name: IELTS Reading Academic Vocabulary
description: Từ vựng học thuật cốt lõi thường gặp trong văn bản nghiên cứu và văn phong học thuật. Nội dung tập trung vào suy luận, mô tả nghiên cứu, quan hệ nguyên nhân–kết quả, so sánh và khoa học tổng quát.

words.example: Many medicines are derived from plants.
words.note: Common in academic texts about origins and sources.

words.example: Children acquire language through interaction.
words.note: Common in education and psychology texts.

words.example: The study revealed a clear difference between the groups.
words.note: Useful when research produces a finding.

words.example: Researchers assessed participants before and after the trial.
words.note: Core academic verb in studies and reports.

words.example: The researchers evaluated the effectiveness of the programme.
words.note: Formal alternative to assess when judging quality or impact.

words.example: The population is estimated to exceed two million.
words.note: Common with numbers, quantities, and future projections.

words.example: The figure approximates the original estimate.
words.note: Useful in quantitative and scientific contexts.

words.example: Scientists must interpret the results carefully.
words.note: Common with data, findings, and evidence.

words.example: Readers can infer the author's attitude from the final paragraph.
words.note: Important reading-skill verb.

words.example: The decline was attributed to rising costs.
words.note: Common in cause-and-effect research writing.

words.example: A new pattern emerged from the data.
words.note: Useful for patterns, trends, species, and ideas becoming visible.

words.example: Subsequent experiments produced similar results.
words.note: Often appears in chronological research descriptions.

words.example: The preceding section outlines the main theory.
words.note: Useful for referencing earlier text.

words.example: The study explored the underlying causes of migration.
words.note: Common for hidden causes, assumptions, or mechanisms.

words.example: The system has inherent limitations.
words.note: Useful for properties that naturally belong to something.

words.example: The laboratory is adjacent to the main research centre.
words.note: Useful for spatial descriptions and diagrams.

words.example: The method was effective, albeit expensive.
words.note: Formal concessive linker common in academic prose.

words.example: The species is widespread across northern regions.
words.note: Useful for describing large geographical prevalence.

words.example: Fresh water is scarce in many arid regions.
words.note: Common with resources and supplies.

words.example: The region has abundant solar energy.
words.note: Opposite of scarce.

words.example: The study provides robust evidence for the theory.
words.note: Common for evidence, methods, and models.

words.example: The researchers proposed a plausible explanation.
words.note: Useful when an explanation seems reasonable but is not proven.

words.mean: thực nghiệm; dựa trên quan sát
words.example: The theory is supported by empirical evidence.
words.note: Core academic adjective for evidence based on observation or experiment.

words.example: The article examines a theoretical framework for learning.
words.note: Useful for distinguishing theory from practice.

words.example: The researchers compared the new method with conventional practice.
words.note: Useful for established or traditional approaches.

words.example: The paper discusses contemporary approaches to urban design.
words.note: Useful for modern practices and current scholarship.

words.example: The preliminary findings require further investigation.
words.note: Common in early-stage research.

words.example: The hypothesis remains controversial among scientists.
words.note: Useful for disputed ideas or evidence.

words.example: The wording of the questionnaire was ambiguous.
words.note: Common when meaning is unclear or open to interpretation.

words.example: The two measures are broadly equivalent.
words.note: Useful for comparing values, functions, or meanings.

words.example: The cumulative effects of pollution are difficult to reverse.
words.note: Common with effects, evidence, and totals.

words.example: The difference was negligible.
words.note: Useful for very small effects or quantities.

words.example: The project required substantial financial support.
words.note: Formal adjective for a large amount or effect.

words.example: The study identifies several prominent factors.
words.note: Useful for important or easily noticed features.

words.example: The two species have distinct characteristics.
words.note: Useful for clear differences between groups or features.

words.example: The process is analogous to that observed in other species.
words.note: Useful in comparisons between similar systems.

words.mean: tạo điều kiện; làm cho dễ hơn
words.example: Technology can facilitate communication between researchers.
words.note: Common academic verb meaning enable or make easier.

words.example: Poor lighting can hinder reading performance.
words.note: Useful for barriers and negative effects.

words.example: The materials undergo several chemical changes.
words.note: Common in process descriptions and scientific texts.

words.example: The solar panels generate enough electricity for the building.
words.note: Useful for energy, ideas, data, and economic activity.

words.example: The species can attain a length of two metres.
words.note: Formal alternative to reach or achieve.

words.example: The material can retain heat for several hours.
words.note: Common in science, memory, and storage contexts.

words.example: The number of participants exceeded expectations.
words.note: Useful for quantities, limits, and targets.

words.example: The sample comprises three distinct groups.
words.note: Formal way to describe components of a whole.

words.example: These three elements constitute the main framework.
words.note: Useful for formal descriptions of components.

words.example: The survey encompasses several areas of public policy.
words.note: Formal alternative to include.

words.example: Climate change may alter migration patterns.
words.note: Useful for significant changes to a condition or system.

words.example: Species must adapt to changing conditions.
words.note: Common in biology, technology, and society texts.

words.example: The problem persisted despite repeated interventions.
words.note: Useful for something continuing over time.

words.example: Exercise can enhance cognitive performance.
words.note: Formal alternative to improve or strengthen.

words.example: The chemical inhibits bacterial growth.
words.note: Common in biology, medicine, and scientific writing.

words.example: A rise in temperature can trigger rapid melting.
words.note: Useful for immediate causes and responses.

words.example: The discovery prompted further investigation.
words.note: Common in research narratives.

words.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in many societies.
words.note: Advanced word for something widespread or almost universal.

words.example: The sample was predominantly female.
words.note: Useful for describing the main characteristic of a group.

words.example: The two groups contained 40 and 60 participants, respectively.
words.note: Important for matching values to previously listed categories.

words.example: The two approaches are fundamentally different.
words.note: Useful for describing essential differences.

words.example: The region is notably warmer in winter.
words.note: Useful for highlighting an important feature.

words.example: The method was expensive; nevertheless, it was effective.
words.note: Formal contrast linker common in academic prose.

words.example: The first group improved, whereas the second showed little change.
words.note: Useful for direct comparison in complex sentences.

words.example: The device reduces heat loss, thereby improving efficiency.
words.note: Useful for showing a result or consequence.

words.example: The roads were flooded, and consequently the event was cancelled.
words.note: Formal result linker.

words.example: The sample was too small, hence the cautious conclusion.
words.note: Formal and concise way to signal a result.

words.example: The article presents evidence from several experiments.
words.note: Core academic noun.

words.example: The researchers tested the hypothesis in two trials.
words.note: Core research term.

words.example: The study uses a theoretical framework.
words.note: Common in social science and academic argument.

words.example: The paper examines the mechanism behind the reaction.
words.note: Useful for explaining how a process works.

words.example: Climate migration is a complex social phenomenon.
words.note: Common academic noun for an observed event or process.

words.example: The region is home to several rare species.
words.note: Common in biology and environmental texts.

words.example: Habitat loss threatens many species.
words.note: High-value environmental and biology word.

words.example: Sleep can affect cognitive performance.
words.note: Common in psychology, education, and neuroscience.

words.example: The study examined dietary habits among adolescents.
words.note: Common in health and nutrition texts.

words.example: The researchers identified a possible genetic factor.
words.note: Common in biology and medicine.

words.example: Archaeological evidence suggests that the settlement was ancient.
words.note: Useful in history and archaeology passages.
